notes: Summary: Lantern runs personalized chat + upsert embeddings for product search. Primary ask: dedicated pool with predictable throughput and hard latency SLOs for user-facing chat.
Workload profile provided: baseline 45 QPS (chat), peak 420 QPS during promo spikes; average prompt size ~300 tokens, response ~120 tokens => ~420 tokens/req peak characteristics.
Throughput targets: steady-state target 40 QPS at p95 <= 120ms; peak target 400 QPS with graceful degradation (p95 <= 350ms acceptable under burst) — engineering asked for concrete GPU reserve plans.
Tokens/sec planning: target sustained tokens/sec ~16k (steady), peak tokens/sec ~168k; asked Redwood to validate with kernel selection/quantization profile and batching strategy.
Model preference: want an open LLM variant (13B-quantized) for cost control; will consider 34B for high-quality personalization flows. Need Redwood to recommend quantization/throughput tradeoffs.
Routing/fallback: require automatic fallback to smaller model tier in case of Dedicated pool saturation; also region failover to EU for a subset of users (data residency).
Security/compliance: strict requirement for SSO/SAML, KMS integration for key management, audit logging for token-level access, 3-year retention controls for logs in designated region.

Commercial asks: SLA with throughput guarantees (X reserved QPS) and financial credits for sustained underperformance; negotiating 99.9% uptime for dedicated service and p95 latency SLA for chat route.

POC plan proposed by AE/SE: two-phase pilot — Phase 1 (2 weeks) run synthetic load to validate baseline QPS and p95 targets on dedicated staging; Phase 2 (4 weeks) ramp with real traffic shadowed and then gradual cutover with canary policies.

Sizing workshop goals: baseline measurement method, recommended GPU types and counts for steady vs peak, autoscaling/burst strategies, expected token/sec per GPU for candidate models, estimated monthly reserved cost.
Quote from Head of ML: "We need predictable tail latency for chat — personalization only pays if latency is stable. If you can't guarantee p95, we can't roll to prod."
Action items for Redwood: deliver model-specific throughput profiles, suggested quantization (4-bit/8-bit) with perf numbers, proposed reserved GPU topology, initial SLA language for review.

Internal Lantern blockers: legal wants explicit data residency clause; infra wants details about VPC peering and allowable egress ranges; finance delaying final approval until pilot metrics validated.
Commercial timeline: Lantern aiming to finalize reserved capacity contract (Q3 start) if pilot meets SLOs; forecasted ARR if committed = $300k-$500k ARR depending on reserved tier.
Risk notes: promotional spikes create large short-term QPS bursts (10x baseline) — workshop must address burst capacity design and cost smoothing (burst credits/burst pools).
Follow-ups: schedule workshop agenda, collect sample token traces from prod (sanitized), confirm on-prem option feasibility for EU-resident subset.
